problem.title: Balance Three Piles
problem.statement: Three piles contain 4, 6, and 8 counters. If the counters are shared equally among the piles, how many counters will each pile contain?
hints: Preserve the total, then divide by the number of piles.

solutionSteps.title: Equal-share the total
solutionSteps.body: The total is 4 + 6 + 8 = 18. Sharing 18 among 3 piles gives a mean of 6.

validationMethods: Independent balance check: move two counters from the 8-pile to the 4-pile, producing 6,6,6; only C matches.
notes: The integer mean reinforces equal-share meaning.

problem.title: Four Summaries
problem.statement: For the ordered data 2, 3, 3, 10, 12, which row correctly gives the median, mode, and range?
hints: Use the middle position, the most frequent value, and maximum minus minimum.

solutionSteps.title: Read each feature
solutionSteps.body: The middle value is 3, the repeated value is 3, and the range is 12 − 2 = 10.

validationMethods: Definition audit gives median 3, mode 3, and range 10.
Independent option-component check: only A has all three values in the requested order.
notes: The mean is intentionally not requested.

problem.title: Recover a Missing Value
problem.statement: Five numbers have mean 8. Four of the numbers are 6, 7, 8, and 9. What is the fifth number?
hints: Use mean × count to recover the total of all five numbers.

solutionSteps.title: Track the total
solutionSteps.body: The total must be 8 × 5 = 40. The known numbers total 30, so the missing number is 40 − 30 = 10.

validationMethods: Independent forward check: (6+7+8+9+10)/5=40/5=8; only C satisfies the stated mean.
notes: The problem makes the hidden total operational.

problem.title: Combine Unequal Groups
problem.statement: A group of 4 students has mean score 70. A group of 6 students has mean score 80. What is the combined mean score?
hints: Recover each group's total score before combining the ten students.

solutionSteps.title: Weight by group size
solutionSteps.body: The totals are 4×70=280 and 6×80=480. Combined, 760 points across 10 students gives a mean of 76.

validationMethods: Independent deviation method: start from 70; six of ten students contribute an extra 10 on average, raising the combined mean by 6 to 76. Only C matches.
notes: Choice B captures the naive unweighted average.

problem.title: Mean after Removing a Value
problem.statement: Six numbers have mean 12. One of the numbers, 17, is removed. What is the mean of the five remaining numbers?
hints: Recover the original total, subtract 17, and update the count.

solutionSteps.title: Update total and count
solutionSteps.body: The original total is 6×12=72. Removing 17 leaves 55 across 5 numbers, so the new mean is 55/5=11.

validationMethods: Independent deviation argument: removing 17, which is 5 above the old mean, reduces the total relative to five copies of 12 by 5, so the new mean is 12−1=11. Only C matches.
notes: Both total and count must be updated.
